body.statement: There exist Markov kernels \(\mathsf K_K^{\to}:\mathcal O_K\rightsquigarrow\mathbb N_0^2\) and \(\mathsf K_K^{\leftarrow}:\mathbb N_0^2\rightsquigarrow\mathcal O_K\), depending only on \(K,n_0,n_1,a,b,r\) and not on \(q\), such that, with the same parameter \(q\in\mathcal R_K^{\circ}(r)\) indexing both experiments, \[\sup_q\lVert P^{\mathrm{mix}}_{K,q}\mathsf K_K^{\to}-P^{\mathcal E}_{\lambda_K,q}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\le e_K,\qquad \sup_q\lVert P^{\mathcal E}_{\lambda_K,q}\mathsf K_K^{\leftarrow}-P^{\mathrm{mix}}_{K,q}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\le e_K,\] where \(e_K=\min\{1,5\varepsilon_K+\eta_K\}\). Both sides attach the decision target \(a-bq\) to the index \(q\). Moreover, for every deterministic array in \(\mathcal T_K(r)\), the law of \((M_K,S_1,\ldots,S_{M_K})\) is within \(e_K^{\mathrm{det}}=\min\{1,5\varepsilon_K+\lambda_K^2/(2K)\}\) in total variation of \(\mathcal E_{\lambda_K,\rho_K}\), uniformly over arrays.
body.justification: Two-sided comparison and uniform deterministic approximation are the information-theoretic bridge from the causal endpoint to a tractable non-Gaussian experiment.
body.gap: Arratia, Goldstein, and Gordon provide forward Poisson approximation, while Kipnis's Theorems~2.1 and~2.3 provide one-sample supported-mixture conditioning and fixed-count transfer; neither supplies two parameter-free marked two-arm kernels on the finite correlation lattice or uniform approximation centered at every realized array target.
body.consumer: Any bounded-loss estimator or interval designed in the marked-Poisson experiment can be transported back to the finite covariate partition with an explicit error budget.
body.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 I_{ik}=\mathbf 1\{Z_{0i}=Z_{1k}\},\qquad
 W=\sum_{i=1}^{n_0}\sum_{k=1}^{n_1}I_{ik}.
\]
For the dependency neighborhood consisting of pairs sharing \(i\) or \(k\), the uniform-cell and arm-independence assumptions give \(\mathbb EI_{ik}=K^{-1}\), and any two distinct indicators in one neighborhood have joint mean \(K^{-2}\).  Thus the quantities in the cited Chen--Stein dependency-neighborhood lemma are
\[
 b_1=\frac{n_0n_1(n_0+n_1-1)}{K^2},\qquad
 b_2=\frac{n_0n_1(n_0+n_1-2)}{K^2}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 d_{\mathrm{TV}}\{\mathcal L(W),\operatorname{Poisson}(\lambda_K)\}
 \le2(b_1+b_2)\le4\varepsilon_K. \tag{1}
\]

Let \(B\) be the event that some cell hit by both arms contains at least three observations in total.  A union bound over two observations from one arm and one from the other yields
\[
 \Pr(B)\le
 \frac{\binom{n_0}{2}n_1+n_0\binom{n_1}{2}}{K^2}
 =\frac{n_0n_1(n_0+n_1-2)}{2K^2}\le\frac{\varepsilon_K}{2}. \tag{2}
\]
On \(B^{\mathrm c}\), every cross-arm matching pair is an exactly-one-per-arm cell, so \(M_K=W\).  Equations (1)--(2) imply
\[
 d_{\mathrm{TV}}\{\mathcal L(M_K),\operatorname{Poisson}(\lambda_K)\}
 \le4\varepsilon_K+\Pr(B). \tag{3}
\]

We next establish the marked factorization, rather than assuming sufficiency.  Under the unconditioned product mixture \(\Gamma_{K,q}\), for an exactly-one-per-arm cell and \(x,y\in\{-1,1\}\), conditional Bernoulli sampling gives
\[
 \Pr_q(X_0=x,X_1=y)
 =\frac14\mathbb E_q[(1+2ax\theta_0)(1+2by\theta_1)]
 =\frac{1+cqxy}{4}. \tag{4}
\]
Therefore \(S=X_0X_1\) has \(\Pr_q(S=s)=(1+cqs)/2\), and, given \(S\), the orientation \(X_0\) is fair and independent of \(q\).  Different one-one cells have independent signs.  A block occupied by only one arm has a law independent of \(q\), even with repeated observations, because the corresponding marginal latent sign is fair.  The occupancy pattern is also parameter free.

Define \(\mathsf K_K^{\to}\) deterministically by retaining \(M_K\) and the positive- and negative-mark counts.  Before shell conditioning, (4) says its law is a count with the parameter-free law of \(M_K\), independently marked with parameter \(q\).  Independent marking is a Markov kernel and therefore contracts total variation.  Shell conditioning changes the latent law, and hence every data pushforward, by exactly at most \(\Gamma_{K,q}(A_{K,q}^{\mathrm c})\le\eta_K\).  From (3),
\[
 \sup_q d_{\mathrm{TV}}\!\left(
 P^{\mathrm{mix}}_{K,q}\mathsf K_K^{\to},P^{\mathcal E}_{\lambda_K,q}
 \right)
 \le4\varepsilon_K+\Pr(B)+\eta_K
 \le5\varepsilon_K+\eta_K. \tag{5}
\]

For the reverse direction, couple an input Poisson count to a variable with the known, parameter-free law of \(M_K\) by assigning common mass \(\min\{\Pr(M_K=m),\Pr(N=m)\}\) at every \(m\), and distribute the two residual masses arbitrarily.  The mismatch probability is their total-variation distance.  Conditional on equality, sample the occupancy configuration from its known law given \(M_K\); assign the input marks to the one-one cells in a uniformly randomized order; sample their fair orientations; and sample all one-arm blocks from their fair-sign mixture.  On \(B\), use any fixed distribution.  Every operation is a finite Markov kernel depending only on the displayed known constants.  By (4), on the event of equal counts and \(B^{\mathrm c}\) this is exactly the unconditioned mixed full-data law.  Hence (3), (2), and then shell conditioning give
\[
 \sup_q d_{\mathrm{TV}}\!\left(
 P^{\mathcal E}_{\lambda_K,q}\mathsf K_K^{\leftarrow},P^{\mathrm{mix}}_{K,q}
 \right)
 \le(4\varepsilon_K+\Pr(B))+\Pr(B)+\eta_K
 \le5\varepsilon_K+\eta_K. \tag{6}
\]
Taking the minimum of the right sides with one proves the two kernel claims.  The target attached to both indexed laws is, by construction, \(a-bq\); the random realized endpoint under the mixture is not being redefined.

Finally fix a deterministic legal array and write \(t_j=\theta_{0j}\theta_{1j}\).  Conditional on \(M_K=m\), a uniform random ordering of the one-one cell labels is sampling without replacement from \(\{1,\ldots,K\}\).  Given label \(j\), conditional outcome independence gives a mark of mean
\[
 \mathbb E(S\mid j)=(2a\theta_{0j})(2b\theta_{1j})=ct_j. \tag{7}
\]
Couple the ordered sample without replacement to \(m\) independent uniform labels.  They agree unless the latter labels repeat, an event of probability at most \(m(m-1)/(2K)\).  Under independent labels, (7) gives independent marks with mean \(cK^{-1}\sum_jt_j=c\rho_K\).  Distinct collision indicators \(I_{ik}\) are pairwise independent, including when they share one observation, and hence
\[
 \mathbb E[M_K(M_K-1)]\le\mathbb E[W(W-1)]
 =\frac{n_0n_1(n_0n_1-1)}{K^2}\le\lambda_K^2. \tag{8}
\]
Averaging the without-replacement coupling error and combining it with (3) gives
\[
 d_{\mathrm{TV}}\!\left(
 \mathcal L_\theta(M_K,S_1,\ldots,S_{M_K}),
 \mathcal E_{\lambda_K,\rho_K}
 \right)
 \le4\varepsilon_K+\Pr(B)+\frac{\lambda_K^2}{2K}
 \le5\varepsilon_K+\frac{\lambda_K^2}{2K}.
\]
This calculation is independent of the particular deterministic signs, proving uniformity.
